questions.q: The higher heating value (HHV) of a fuel assumes that:
c: Water formed is condensed to liquid
questions.e: HHV includes the latent heat of the water vapor, which is recovered when the water condenses to liquid.

questions.q: What is the primary constituent of natural gas?
questions.e: Natural gas is mostly methane (CH4), typically 85–95%.

questions.q: What is the reason producer gas requiring more air than natural gas?
questions.e: Producer gas has a much lower heating value, so a larger volume of gas (and its combustion air) is needed for the same heat output. Marked answer on the paper.

questions.q: The Orsat apparatus is used to measure:
questions.e: The Orsat apparatus analyzes flue gas by absorbing CO₂, O₂ and CO in turn.

questions.q: The main cause of smoke in combustion is:
questions.e: Not enough air means incomplete combustion, so unburned carbon shows up as smoke.

questions.q: In boiler combustion, a low CO₂ percentage with high O₂ indicates:
questions.e: Extra air dilutes the flue gas, which lowers the CO₂ percentage and raises the O₂.

questions.q: ASTM D240 is the standard test for:
c: Heat of combustion of liquid hydrocarbons
questions.e: ASTM D240 measures the heat of combustion of liquid hydrocarbon fuels with a bomb calorimeter.

questions.q: Which solid fuel generally has the highest volatile matter?
questions.e: Peat is the lowest-rank solid fuel, so it has the highest volatile matter (anthracite has the lowest).

questions.q: For safe storage of liquid fuels, the container should be:
questions.e: The container must be sealed to limit vapor escape but vented so pressure from temperature changes can be released.

questions.q: The ASTM standard for coal proximate analysis is:
questions.e: ASTM D3172 covers proximate analysis of coal and coke (moisture, volatile matter, fixed carbon, ash).

questions.q: What is meant by “variable load” in a power plant?
c: Fluctuation in electrical demand over time
questions.e: Variable load is the change in electrical demand on the plant over time.

questions.q: Given two plants of similar capacity where one has lower load demand and the other has higher load demand. Which plant operates more efficiently?
questions.e: A higher load factor means the plant runs closer to its rated capacity, so it is used more fully and efficiently.

questions.q: Which control method is commonly used to match generation with variable electrical load?
questions.e: Automatic generation control (AGC) adjusts generator output to follow changing demand.

questions.q: What is “spinning reserve” in variable load management?
c: Reserve of fuel oil in storage tanks
Backup capacity kept running and synchronized
questions.e: Spinning reserve is generating capacity that is already online and synchronized, ready to pick up load quickly.

questions.q: What is “load factor” in power plant economics?
c: Ratio of maximum demand to average demand
Ratio of average load to maximum demand
Ratio of base load to peak load
Ratio of installed capacity to connected load
questions.e: Load factor = average load / maximum (peak) demand over a period.

questions.q: What is the relation between variable load operation and plant maintenance cost?
questions.e: Frequent load changes cause thermal and mechanical cycling, which increases wear and maintenance cost.

questions.q: What is the main purpose of peak-load plants in a variable load system?
c: To provide base power at constant rate
To supply extra power during demand peaks
To dry the fuel before combustion
questions.e: Peak-load plants (such as gas turbines or diesel sets) run only when demand is high.

questions.q: Which type of control valve is preferred for fast response in variable load steam lines?
questions.e: Marked answer on the paper. Globe valves give good throttling and control of flow, which is why they are used in control service.

questions.q: What happens to generator excitation when load increases?
questions.e: More load drops the terminal voltage, so excitation must increase to hold voltage.

questions.q: What is the term for rapid decrease in load due to sudden disconnection of a major consumer?
questions.e: Load rejection is the sudden loss of load on a generator.

questions.q: Which law of thermodynamics defines the concept of temperature?
questions.e: The zeroth law (thermal equilibrium) is the basis for temperature.

questions.q: Which property is an intensive property of a system?
questions.e: Intensive properties do not depend on the amount of matter. Temperature is intensive; the others are extensive.

questions.q: What is an example of an extensive property?
questions.e: Extensive properties depend on system size, as volume does.

questions.q: What is the term for a system that can exchange energy but not mass with its surroundings?
questions.e: A closed system exchanges energy (heat or work) but no mass.

questions.q: Which thermodynamic property is a measure of disorder?
questions.e: Entropy measures molecular disorder (randomness).

questions.q: Which type of system does not exchange either mass or energy with its surroundings?
questions.e: An isolated system exchanges neither mass nor energy.

questions.q: What does the second law of thermodynamics establish?
questions.e: The second law gives the direction of natural processes. Heat flows from hot to cold without outside work.

questions.q: What is the term for the energy that can be converted into work?
questions.e: Exergy (available energy) is the maximum useful work obtainable.

questions.q: What is the relation between internal energy and enthalpy change for constant pressure processes?
questions.e: From h = u + pv at constant p: Δh = Δu + pΔv.

questions.q: What parameters are inversely related when enthalpy is constant?
questions.e: Marked answer on the paper: pressure and volume. In a constant-enthalpy (throttling) process, an increase in one goes with a decrease in the other.

questions.q: What parameter primarily affects Diesel cycle efficiency?
questions.e: Marked answer on the paper. Diesel cycle efficiency depends on compression ratio and cut-off ratio, and of the choices given only cut-off ratio is a cycle parameter.

questions.q: What determines the mean effective pressure in an engine cycle?
questions.e: mep = net work per cycle / displacement volume, so work per cycle is the determining factor.

questions.q: Which device regulates the air-fuel mixture in a carbureted SI engine?
questions.e: The carburetor meters fuel into the air stream in a carbureted engine.

questions.q: Which cycle efficiency depends only on compression ratio?
questions.e: Otto efficiency = 1 − 1/r^(k−1), which depends only on compression ratio (and k).

questions.q: What is the main advantage of a two-stroke engine over a four-stroke engine?
c: More power output per unit weight
questions.e: A two-stroke fires every revolution, giving a higher power-to-weight ratio.

questions.q: Which engine efficiency is always lower than the air-standard efficiency?
questions.e: Brake efficiency includes all losses (combustion, heat, friction), so it is the lowest. Marked answer on the paper.

questions.q: What does the term “stoichiometric air-fuel ratio” mean?
c: Maximum air supply to minimize power
Minimum air required for complete combustion
Exact air required for complete combustion
Excess air supplied to reduce emissions
questions.e: Stoichiometric means the exact (theoretical) amount of air needed to burn the fuel completely, with no excess.

questions.q: What is the effect of increasing compression ratio in SI engines?
questions.e: Otto efficiency rises with compression ratio (until knock limits it).

questions.q: Which type of scavenging is used in most two-stroke engines?
questions.e: Loop scavenging is the most common design in two-stroke engines. (The handwriting on your paper for this one was hard to read, so please check it.)

questions.q: What is the effect of increasing cut-off ratio in a Diesel cycle?
questions.e: A larger cut-off ratio means heat is added over more of the stroke, which lowers Diesel cycle efficiency.

questions.q: What is the basic mode of heat transfer in solids?
questions.e: Heat moves through solids mainly by conduction.

questions.q: What law states that heat flux is proportional to the negative temperature gradient?
questions.e: Fourier's law: q = −k·dT/dx.

questions.q: What heat transfer law states that heat transfer is proportional to temperature difference?
questions.e: Newton's law of cooling: q = hA(Ts − T∞).

questions.q: What factor directly affects convective heat transfer?
questions.e: Higher fluid velocity thins the boundary layer and changes the convection coefficient.

questions.q: What happens to the convection heat transfer coefficient when air velocity increases?
questions.e: Faster flow thins the boundary layer, so h goes up.

questions.q: Which non-dimensional number compares conduction resistance to convection resistance?
questions.e: Bi = hL/k is the ratio of internal conduction resistance to surface convection resistance.

questions.q: Which boundary condition represents constant surface temperature?
questions.e: The Dirichlet (first-kind) condition specifies the surface temperature.

questions.q: What is the mechanism of heat transfer in fluids due to bulk motion?
questions.e: Convection is heat transfer carried by the bulk motion of a fluid.

questions.q: Which type of convection occurs when a fan is used to cool a heated surface?
questions.e: A fan moves the fluid externally, which is forced convection.

questions.q: Which dimensionless number is used to calculate radiative heat transfer between surfaces?
questions.e: Marked answer on the paper. The view factor and radiation shape factor are the same geometric quantity (F12), so check which one your reviewer prefers.
